scope: Offline fixed-corpus English, Spanish and Hindi retrieval/review; no production connector.
license: CC-BY-SA-4.0 data; independently written workflow code Apache-2.0.

rights.retrieval: Explicit bounded no-key downloads of three fixed files at upstream Git revision 7d30520c717524000f0d9d2f9c10a069acd9d285; verify pinned SHA-256.
rights.retention: Raw translated Wikipedia passages, indexes, review packets, credentials and personal assessor mappings remain local and ignored; retain attribution and version provenance.
rights.display: Local assessors may inspect attributed snapshot passages; offline forms make no third-party requests. Public reports contain identifiers and aggregate coverage/metrics.
rights.redistribution: Selected queries and answer-context mappings are adaptations under CC-BY-SA-4.0 with attribution, source links and change notices. No raw passage bundle or private human judgments are published automatically. Corpus identifiers do not relicense Wikipedia article content.
rights.evaluation: Use professional translations and original crowdworker questions as fixed-corpus inputs. Distinguish QA answer-context mapping from human retrieval relevance. Separately identify AI-authored draft intent probes.
rights.training: No training or feedback-driven production change. Holdout groups are reserved from project tuning; future data/model use needs a separate decision.

attribution: XQuAD: Mikel Artetxe, Sebastian Ruder and Dani Yogatama, On the Cross-lingual Transferability of Monolingual Representations (2020). SQuAD: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev and Percy Liang (2016). Original article passages: Wikipedia contributors; translations: XQuAD contributors.
limitations: Historical Wikipedia snapshot and selected questions; no current-web, original-source, freshness or population-representativeness claim.
English, Spanish and Hindi only; translated instances share groups and are not independent samples of user demand.
A relevant answer-bearing parent paragraph is a derived QA mapping, not an exhaustive relevance judgment.
Only real, consented assessors can provide new human judgments; script attestation cannot prove a person's identity or independence.
